claims.text: The starting FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are solid and chemically homogeneous or near-homogeneous FCC or BCC solid solutions.
Preferential Cu segregation to the nanoparticle surface governs the onset and progression of the phase transition.
Cu has a lower melting point than the other constituent elements.
Cu has lower cohesive energy than the other constituent elements.
When heated, Cu atoms preferentially migrate to or remain at the nanoparticle surface.
The local atomic environment of nanoparticle surface atoms can affect their surface energy and stability.
Cu accumulation at the surface reduces the local cohesive or effective surface energy.
Reduced atomic coordination at the nanoparticle exterior contributes to lowering its local melting point.
Surface Cu enrichment lowers the melting point of the surface region and initiates premelting.
Surface-initiated premelting propagates gradually inward and drives the overall phase transformation.
Nanoparticles with enhanced Cu surface segregation will have a lower premelting onset temperature than uniformly mixed controls.
A liquid-like or disordered layer will first form at Cu-enriched surfaces.
The liquid-like or disordered surface layer will progress inward during continued heating.
The proposed mechanism is most important for nanoparticles with a high surface-to-volume ratio.
Changes in particle size or synthesis conditions that alter diffusion kinetics can change the observed melting behavior.
An inert atmosphere is required to prevent oxidation during the heating comparison.

contradictions.description: The conditions require identical initial compositional homogeneity, whereas the comparison is described as one sample intentionally prepared to promote or possess enhanced Cu surface segregation and a control expected to remain homogeneous. If enhanced segregation is already present before heating, the initial elemental distributions are not identical; the design must instead distinguish identical initial distributions with different segregation kinetics from deliberately different initial surface compositions.
